case_name: Akshat Commercial Pvt. Ltd. & Anr vs Kalpana Chakraborty & Ors
facts_of_case: The property involved was sold by the Allahabad Bank and purchased by the present appellants. The writ-petitioner disputed the legality of the notice under Section 13(4) of the SARFAESI Act and moved this High Court.

legal_principles.principle: Proceedings under Section 17 of the SARFAESI Act are not appellate proceedings, but initial actions brought before a forum.
legal_principles.held: It seems to be a misnomer. In fact it is the initial action which is brought before a forum as prescribed under the Act, raising grievance against the action or measures taken by one of the parties to the contract.
cited_cases: Mardia Chemicals Ltd. & Anr. vs. Union of India & Ors., (2004) 4 SCC 311
M/s. Transcore vs. Union of India & Anr., AIR 2007 SC 712
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in understanding the nature of SARFAESI Act proceedings

legal_principles.principle: The marginal note to Section 17(1) of the SARFAESI Act cannot control the text content of Section 17(1).
legal_principles.held: It is true that, the marginal note states that Section 17(1) is a right to appeal. In our view, the marginal note to Section 17(1) cannot control the text and the content of Section17 (1) which, as stated above, states that the borrower aggrieved by any of the measures in Section 13(4) may make an application to the DRT.
cited_cases: Mardia Chemicals Ltd. & Anr. vs. Union of India & Ors., (2004) 4 SCC 311
M/s. Transcore vs. Union of India & Anr., AIR 2007 SC 712
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — significance in understanding the interpretation of Section 17(1) of the SARFAESI Act

outcome.final_order: The order dated May 5th and 6th, 2008 passed by a learned Single Judge of this Court was set aside.

use_for_drafting: guidelines for writ applications in family law cases
